title: Moroni writes and seals the record
summary: Moroni writes to his brethren, the Lamanites, noting the years since the sign of Christ’s coming, and says he seals the records after his exhortation.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni writes to his brethren, the Lamanites, and says more than four hundred and twenty years have passed since the sign of Christ’s coming.
Moroni says he seals the records after speaking words of exhortation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni is writing; records are present with him.
unspecified_visual_details: Moroni’s appearance, writing implements, records’ appearance, and surroundings.

narration.text: Now I, Moroni, write somewhat as seemeth me good
And I seal up these records

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the sign of Christ’s coming as a present event.

title: Remember and ponder
summary: Moroni exhorts readers to remember the Lord’s mercy and ponder it in their hearts when they read the record.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni exhorts readers to remember the Lord’s mercy to humanity from Adam’s creation until they receive the record, and to ponder it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni’s exhortation can be presented as off-screen narration over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The readers’ identities, appearance, and location; any depiction of Adam or the history of humanity.

narration.text: remember how merciful the Lord hath been
ponder it in your hearts.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse refers broadly to past and future readers; it does not narrate those historical events as present scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a sequence of humanity’s history as events occurring now.

title: Ask God in faith
summary: Moroni exhorts readers to ask God whether the record is true, promising that the Holy Ghost can manifest truth and enable them to know it.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni exhorts readers to ask God, in Christ’s name, with a sincere heart, real intent, and faith in Christ; he says God will manifest the truth by the power of the Holy Ghost.
Moroni says that by the power of the Holy Ghost people may know the truth of all things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use Moroni’s voice as off-screen narration rather than depicting a recipient or a supernatural manifestation.
unspecified_visual_details: Any person receiving the record, the manner of asking, and any visible form or appearance of the Holy Ghost.

narration.text: ask God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Christ
ye may know the truth of all things.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promised manifestation is not described as a visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible Holy Ghost or an answer to a particular reader.

title: Good acknowledges Christ
summary: Moroni teaches that what is good is just and true and acknowledges Christ; he exhorts readers not to deny God’s power.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni teaches that what is good is just and true and does not deny Christ, but acknowledges that he is.
Moroni says people may know Christ is by the power of the Holy Ghost and exhorts them not to deny God’s power, which works according to human faith.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the teaching as off-screen narration over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible depiction of Christ, God’s power, or the Holy Ghost.

narration.text: whatsoever thing is good is just and true
deny not the power of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses teach about divine power; they do not describe a visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a miracle or divine figure not described in the text.

title: Gifts of God
summary: Moroni exhorts his brethren not to deny God’s many gifts, which are administered in different ways by the same God through manifestations of the Spirit for people’s benefit.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says God’s gifts are many, come from the same God, are administered in different ways, and are given by manifestations of the Spirit to benefit people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration; the verse supports no particular gift being visibly exercised here.
unspecified_visual_details: The people receiving gifts and the particular forms of any manifestations.

narration.text: deny not the gifts of God
to profit them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The gifts are taught about, not shown as specific events in this verse.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a recipient, gift, or miraculous display.

title: Wisdom and knowledge
summary: Moroni describes gifts of teaching the word of wisdom and teaching the word of knowledge by the Spirit.

explicit_facts.text: One person may receive the gift of teaching the word of wisdom by the Spirit of God.
Another may receive the gift of teaching the word of knowledge by the same Spirit.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can remain off-screen narration; no recipients are specified.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity, appearance, location, and actions of any gifted people.

narration.text: teach the word of wisdom
teach the word of knowledge

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses list gifts without narrating particular people exercising them.
prohibited_inventions: Do not create visible teachers or learners as specific characters.

title: Faith, healing, and miracles
summary: Moroni lists gifts of exceedingly great faith, healing, and working mighty miracles.

explicit_facts.text: The gifts include exceedingly great faith and gifts of healing by the same Spirit.
Another gift is the ability to work mighty miracles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration rather than visualizing unspecified healings or miracles.
unspecified_visual_details: Recipients, circumstances, and appearances of any healing or miracle.

narration.text: exceedingly great faith
the gifts of healing
work mighty miracles

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The gifts are named, not enacted in the verses.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a healing or miracle scene.

title: Prophecy and ministering spirits
summary: Moroni lists prophesying concerning all things and beholding angels and ministering spirits as gifts.

explicit_facts.text: One gift is to prophesy concerning all things.
Another gift is beholding angels and ministering spirits.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Keep the description as off-screen narration; no angel or spirit is visibly described in this scene.
unspecified_visual_details: The recipient and any appearance of angels or ministering spirits.

narration.text: prophesy concerning all things
the beholding of angels and ministering spirits

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse names a gift of beholding; it does not narrate an angelic appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict angels or ministering spirits as present.

title: Tongues and interpretation
summary: Moroni lists gifts of tongues and interpretation of languages and different kinds of tongues.

explicit_facts.text: One gift is all kinds of tongues.
Another gift is interpretation of languages and different kinds of tongues.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration; the verses do not specify a particular speaker or setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The recipients, languages, and circumstances of these gifts.

narration.text: all kinds of tongues
the interpretation of languages

doctrinal_or_story_notes: No specific utterance or interpretation is narrated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue in another language.

title: The gifts come through Christ
summary: Moroni says the gifts come by the Spirit of Christ, are given severally, and exhorts his brethren to remember that every good gift comes from Christ and that the gifts endure according to belief.

explicit_facts.text: All the gifts come by the Spirit of Christ and come to each person severally according to Christ’s will.
Moroni exhorts his brethren to remember that every good gift comes from Christ.
Moroni says Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and spiritual gifts will not cease while the world stands except according to human unbelief.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Keep the teaching as off-screen narration over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible giver, recipient, or depiction of spiritual gifts.

narration.text: every good gift cometh of Christ.
the same yesterday, today, and forever

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is teaching about gifts and their continuance, not a narrated display of them.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ distributing gifts or invent a visible manifestation.

title: Faith, hope, and charity
summary: Moroni teaches that faith entails hope and hope entails charity, and that faith, hope, and charity are necessary for salvation in the kingdom of God.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni teaches that where there is faith there must be hope, and where there is hope there must be charity.
Moroni teaches that without charity, faith, or hope, a person cannot be saved in the kingdom of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the teaching through off-screen narration.
unspecified_visual_details: Any people or symbols used to illustrate faith, hope, or charity.

narration.text: there must also be hope
there must also be charity.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses state teachings rather than describing visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the kingdom of God as a specific visible setting.

title: Hope, despair, and faith
summary: Moroni says lack of hope leads to despair, which comes because of iniquity, and recalls Christ’s words that faith enables people to do what is expedient unto him.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says that without hope a person must be in despair, and despair comes because of iniquity.
Moroni attributes to Christ the teaching that with faith people can do all things expedient unto him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Keep both teachings as off-screen narration, without visualizing despair or deeds not specified.
unspecified_visual_details: The people addressed and any specific acts described as expedient.

narration.text: despair cometh because of iniquity.
If ye have faith ye can do all things

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni reports Christ’s teaching; Christ is not described as visibly present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Christ speaking in person.

title: Warning about unbelief
summary: Moroni addresses the ends of the earth, warning that if God’s power and gifts cease among them it will be because of unbelief, and warns against doing them away and dying in sin.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says that if God’s power and gifts are done away among the people, it will be because of unbelief.
Moroni says that if someone among them does good, that person works by God’s power and gifts.
Moroni warns those who do these things away and die that they die in their sins and cannot be saved in the kingdom of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use Moroni’s voice as off-screen narration; no people’s actions are individually specified.
unspecified_visual_details: The people addressed and any particular act of rejecting gifts.

narration.text: it shall be because of unbelief.
he shall work by the power and gifts of God.
they die in their sins

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The warnings are conditional teachings, not a narrated death or judgment scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific person dying or being judged.

title: Moroni’s future witness
summary: Moroni exhorts readers to remember his words and says they will see him at God’s bar, where the Lord God will ask whether he declared the written words to them.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni exhorts readers to remember these things and says they will see him at the bar of God.
Moroni says the Lord God will ask whether he declared the words written by this man, like one crying from the dead or speaking out of the dust.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show Moroni as the present speaker; the future bar of God is described as a future event, not the current moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and location of the bar of God, and any future participants.

narration.text: for ye shall see me at the bar of God
like as one crying from the dead

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future encounter is referenced, not narrated as happening now.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the bar of God or God speaking in a present-tense scene.

title: Words proceed from God
summary: Moroni declares that the prophecies will be fulfilled, that God’s word will proceed from generation to generation, and that God will show the writing is true.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni declares these things unto the fulfilling of the prophecies and says God’s word will proceed from generation to generation.
Moroni says God will show that what he has written is true.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner in which God will show the writing is true and the generations addressed.

narration.text: his word shall hiss forth from generation to generation.
that that which I have written is true.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse uses figurative wording; it does not describe a visible voice or sound.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the word literally hissing or proceeding as a visible supernatural object.

title: Come unto Christ
summary: Moroni exhorts readers to come unto Christ, lay hold on every good gift, and avoid the evil gift and unclean thing.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni exhorts readers to come unto Christ, lay hold on every good gift, and touch not the evil gift or unclean thing.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The exhortation can be conveyed as off-screen narration; the commands need not be shown as literal objects or actions.
unspecified_visual_details: What the gifts or unclean thing look like, and any recipients.

narration.text: come unto Christ, and lay hold upon every good gift
touch not the evil gift

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The exhortation is figurative and doctrinal; no actual objects are described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict good or evil gifts as physical objects or invent Christ’s appearance.

title: Awake and arise, Jerusalem
summary: Moroni quotes an exhortation addressed to Jerusalem to awake, arise from the dust, put on beautiful garments, strengthen its stakes, and enlarge its borders, in fulfillment of the Eternal Father’s covenants with the house of Israel.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni exhorts Jerusalem to awake and arise from the dust, put on beautiful garments, strengthen its stakes, and enlarge its borders.
Moroni connects this exhortation with fulfillment of the Eternal Father’s covenants to the house of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Keep the exhortation as off-screen narration; Jerusalem is an addressed figure in the quoted language, not a specified visible person.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Jerusalem as a person, garments, stakes, borders, and the house of Israel.

narration.text: awake, and arise from the dust, O Jerusalem
put on thy beautiful garments

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The language is an exhortation, not a narrated scene of Jerusalem physically rising.
prohibited_inventions: Do not personify Jerusalem as a visible character or depict a literal rebuilding.

title: Perfected in Christ
summary: Moroni exhorts readers to come unto Christ, deny ungodliness, and love God, teaching that God’s grace can make them perfect and sanctified in Christ, through Christ’s blood, unto remission of sins.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni exhorts readers to come unto Christ, be perfected in him, deny ungodliness, and love God with all their might, mind, and strength.
Moroni teaches that God’s grace is sufficient, that people may be perfect in Christ, and that they cannot deny God’s power if perfected in Christ by grace.
Moroni teaches that people are sanctified in Christ by God’s grace through Christ’s blood in the Father’s covenant, unto remission of sins, becoming holy and without spot.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the passage through off-screen narration rather than a visual depiction of atonement or sanctification.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible form of grace, sanctification, or Christ’s blood.

narration.text: come unto Christ, and be perfected in him
that ye become holy, without spot.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses teach about grace, perfection, sanctification, and remission; they do not narrate Christ’s suffering as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the crucifixion, wounds, blood, or a supernatural transformation.

title: Moroni’s farewell
summary: Moroni bids farewell, says he soon goes to rest in the paradise of God until his spirit and body reunite, and describes being brought forth triumphantly to meet his audience before the Eternal Judge.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni bids all farewell and says he soon goes to rest in the paradise of God until his spirit and body reunite.
Moroni says he will be brought forth triumphant through the air to meet his audience before the Eternal Judge of the living and the dead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show Moroni as the present speaker; his future rest and reunion are described, not occurring in this moment.
unspecified_visual_details: Moroni’s surroundings, the appearance of paradise, the reunion, and the Eternal Judge.

narration.text: And now I bid unto all, farewell.
I soon go to rest in the paradise of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni describes future events; the verse does not narrate his death or the future meeting as present action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moroni’s death, bodily reunion, or the Eternal Judge appearing now.
